questions.question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: All beaches are sand. Some deserts are sand. All mountains are rocky. Conclusions: (I) At least some beaches are desert. (II) At least some sands are rocky.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to
be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given
statements.
Statements:
All beaches are sand.
Some deserts are sand.
All mountains are rocky.
Conclusions:
(I) At least some beaches are desert.
(II) At least some sands are rocky.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. At least some beaches are desert → Does not follow (As all beaches are sand and some deserts are sand. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. At least some sands are rocky → Does not follow (As all beaches are sand, some deserts are sand and all mountains are rocky. So it is possible but not definite.)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

questions.question: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: No medicine is a capsule. Some capsules are tablets. Some tablets are laptops. Conclusions: I. Some capsules are laptops. II. All tablets can never be medicines.
questions.questionHtml:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements.

Statements:

No medicine is a capsule.

Some capsules are tablets.

Some tablets are laptops.

Conclusions:

I. Some capsules are laptops.

II. All tablets can never be medicines.

options.text: Neither Conclusion I nor II follow.
options.html: Neither Conclusion I nor II follow.

options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow.
options.html: Both Conclusions I and II follow.

questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. Some capsules are laptops → Does not follow (As some capsules are tablets and some tablets are laptops. So it is possible but not definite.)

II. All tablets can never be medicines → Follow (As no medicine is a capsule and some capsules are tablets. As no direct relation is given between medicine and tablets, therefore it is false.)

∴ Here, Only Conclusion II follows.

questions.question: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.questionHtml: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution:
1) Total triangles = [Number of parts × (1 + Number of parts)] ÷ 2

= [2 × (1 + 2)] ÷ 2

= [2 × 3] ÷ 2

= 6 ÷ 2

= 3

As there are 2 same types of triangles, therefore total number of triangles will be (3 × 2) = 6 

2) As marked there are total 12 triangles.

Thus, there are total (6 + 12) = 18 triangles.

interchanged
93 – 7 ÷ 65 × 13 + 34 = ?
questions.solution:
Given equation: 93 - 7 ÷ 65 × 13 + 34 = ?

Now, if ‘+’ and ‘-‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged, then:

⇒ 93 + 7 × 65 ÷ 13 - 34 = ? ⇒ 93 +  7 × 5 - 34 = ?

⇒ 93 + 35 - 34 = ? ⇒ 128 - 34 = 94.

questions.question: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.questionHtml:
Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out.
(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
Option 1) 11 – 882

The logic followed here is: (First Number  × 8) × First Number = Second Number

(11 × 8) × 11 = 882

88 × 11 = 882

968 ≠ 882 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Thus, out of all the options '11 – 882' is the odd one out.
